title: Diagnose a worse position: weakness and threat, one sentence each
outcomes: States the four questions of the defender
Writes the chief weakness and the chief threat of a position in one sentence each
Compares the candidate moves that stop a threat instead of playing the first one
Applies the routine to a position from his own games in My games

steps.text:
Four questions for the side that is worse.
1. What is my **chief weakness**?
2. What is the opponent's **chief threat**?
3. Is his advantage big enough to win by force?
4. Will it be settled in the middlegame or the ending?
This lesson practises questions 1 and 2 only; the app does not teach 3 and 4 yet. Aim to get back the power to choose your own moves; do not give up early.

steps.prompt: Write the chief weakness and the chief threat of that position, one sentence each. Compare them with the explanation you just saw.

steps.text: A move that stops the threat is the first answer. Several moves can do it, and the engine may rate one far lower. Before you parry, compare the candidates: which one leaves your weak square better protected and your pieces freer? That comparison is a *rule of thumb*, not a proof.

steps.title: Parry, plan, or lost
steps.prompt: The first position has a move that answers the threat for good. Predict what a second parry does, and what changes when the disadvantage is overwhelming.

Open My games and load a game you lost or struggled in. In Step 1, step to the moment where you felt most worried and write, in the boxes below, the chief weakness and the chief threat there. Then press Analyse with the engine and check whether that moment is among the biggest drops. What did you miss, if anything?

fields.label: After the analysis: what did you miss, if anything?

steps.prompt: Think of the position you diagnosed first. Which was harder to name in one sentence, the weakness or the threat? How sure were you of that sentence? (low / medium / high)

sources: authored items IBa2-16 to IBa2-19, IBa2-21, IBa2-22 (batch a2); the learner's own games in My games
